## Definition
A ***spanning tree*** in a graph is a subgraph containing all vertices, which is isomorphic to a tree.

## Remark
A graph is connected $\iff$ it has a spanning tree.

## Algorithm
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $T$ be an "empty" connected subgraph of $G$, with $V(T) = \{ v_0 \}$. Let $R := V(G) \setminus V(T)$. 

For $i = 1, 2, ..., n-1$, 

**(i)** find a vertex $t \in V(T)$ and $v_i \in R$ such that $t \sim v_i$. (There is always some edge from $T$ to $R$ as $G$ is connected.)

**(ii)** Remove $v_i$ from $R$ and add a vertex $v_i$ and an edge $\{ t, v_i \}$ to $T$. 

The algorithm must terminate in the finite number of steps, because $R$ is finite. Note that $T$ is always a tree, and when the algorithm is finished, it is spanning. 

# Reference
- Matousek, J., & Nesetril, J. (2008). Invitation to Discrete Mathematics. Oxford University Press.
